newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: INTERVIEW - OUB treasury operations growing.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - OUB treasury operations growing.

text.p: Overseas Union Bank Ltd's treasury operations, such as trading in currencies, derivatives and commodities on the bank's own account, are growing, president and chief executive officer Peter Seah said on Friday.

He told Reuters in an interview he expected treasury operations to become an increasingly important part of the activities of Singapore financial institutions but banks had to position themselves well to take advantage of the trend.
"For us, our treasury operations have been growing and it is a significant percentage of our total bottom line," Seah said.

"Our treasury income (now) contributes more than 10 percent of our total income," Seah said. "Contributions from treasury fluctuate from year to year. But overall the contributions have stayed pretty much at more than 10 percent."
Seah said OUB, one of Singapore's four main banks with assets at the end of 1995 of Singapore $25.63 billion, stood to benefit from the growth of Singapore as a major financial trading centre.

"We are a major player in both the foreign exchange market and the futures and derivatives market in SIMEX (Singapore International Monetary Exchange) and we see that area of income as continuing to grow," he said.

"But we also of course realise that it is an area that needs to be closely managed. And that is something that we have been addressing in terms of strengthening our risk management capabilities," he added.
